original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:38-39 (E16 S4 test): in a two-asset channel with one asset's token made to revert on transfer, transfer(assetIndex) still pays the other asset, and transferAllAssets reverts as a whole.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. On integrated df56543, test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol (arn-bfc): test_transfer_assetIndex_paysOtherAsset_whenPairedTokenReverts calls adjudicator.transfer(0, ...) and asserts only adjudicator.holdings(usdc, channelId) == 0 and adjudicator.holdings(revToken, channelId) == HUB_FUNDS (lines 87-91); it reads no recipient's token balance. test_transferAllAssets_revertsAsWhole_whenPairedTokenReverts uses vm.expectRevert() with no reason (line 113) before transferAllAssets. No search was made for a mutation that these tests miss.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. 1. Read test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol:66-121 at df56543.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol
restatement: Two regression tests in test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol check the per-asset-exit invariant for the adjudicator contract. The first test, test_transfer_assetIndex_paysOtherAsset_whenPairedTokenReverts, calls adjudicator.transfer(0, channelId, outcomeBytes, stateHash, new uint256[](0)). It currently asserts only adjudicator.holdings(usdc, channelId) == 0 and adjudicator.holdings(revToken, channelId) == HUB_FUNDS (lines 90-91). It never reads the custodian's real USDC token balance. A defect that clears the internal ledger without a real payment would still pass this test undetected. The fix adds an assertion that the custodian's real USDC balance increases by exactly HUB_FUNDS (100e6) when transfer(0, ...) runs. The second test, test_transferAllAssets_revertsAsWhole_whenPairedTokenReverts, currently expects any revert through a bare vm.expectRevert() (line 113) before adjudicator.transferAllAssets(channelId, state.outcome, stateHash) runs. A revert for any unrelated cause would still pass this test undetected. The fix replaces the bare revert expectation with the exact reason 'RevertingTransferToken: transfer blocked'. Both changes are confined to the test file; they do not touch adjudicator production code.

restatement_clauses.text: test_transfer_assetIndex_paysOtherAsset_whenPairedTokenReverts (test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol:67-92) calls adjudicator.transfer(0, channelId, outcomeBytes, stateHash, new uint256[](0)) and currently asserts only adjudicator.holdings(usdc, channelId) == 0 and adjudicator.holdings(revToken, channelId) == HUB_FUNDS (lines 90-91); it must instead also prove the USDC actually reached the custodian, by asserting the custodian's real USDC token balance increases by HUB_FUNDS (100e6) when transfer(0, ...) runs.

test_transferAllAssets_revertsAsWhole_whenPairedTokenReverts (test/PerAssetExitS4.t.sol:95-119) currently expects any revert with a bare, reason-less vm.expectRevert() (line 113) before adjudicator.transferAllAssets(channelId, state.outcome, stateHash); it must instead expect the exact revert reason 'RevertingTransferToken: transfer blocked', so a revert for any other cause does not pass the test.

goal: Strengthen the two S4 regression tests so each one proves the real, externally visible outcome. The first test must prove a real USDC payment to the custodian's wallet. The second test must prove the one specific blocked-token revert reason, not any revert.
acceptance_criteria: Someone reading the first test sees it record the custodian's real USDC wallet balance twice: once before the single-asset payout, once after.
Running the single-asset payout test against the real adjudicator, custodian, and token contracts still shows a pass, confirming the custodian's balance really rose by the full HUB_FUNDS amount.
Someone reading the second test sees it expect the exact wording 'RevertingTransferToken: transfer blocked' before the whole-channel payout call.
Someone reading the second test no longer finds a bare revert expectation with no stated reason before the whole-channel payout call.
Running the whole-channel payout test against the real adjudicator, custodian, and token contracts still shows a pass, confirming the one stated reason really is the reason the call fails.
